q: Which statement is true?
o: Combined cut-and-fill is the costliest grading
Climate directly affects people's well-being and attitudes, and these shape planning needs
An isolated building is surrounded by structures
n: Climate directly affects people's comfort, well-being and attitudes, which shape planning needs. The other statements are false. Balanced cut-and-fill is usually the cheapest grading, not the costliest. Source: Olgyay, Design with Climate; Lynch & Hack, Site Planning.

q: Which restoration approach preserves an object without touching its material, by preventing agents of decay?
n: Static (preventive) restoration preserves an object without altering its material, by controlling the agents of decay. Anastylosis reassembles fallen original parts. Source: Feilden, Conservation of Historic Buildings; ICOMOS Venice Charter.

q: Which survey technique for mid- to large-scale projects reads the genius loci to guide future development?
n: Historical analysis reads a site's genius loci (its evolution and character) to guide future development on mid- to large-scale projects. Source: Norberg-Schulz, Genius Loci; Bentley et al., Responsive Environments.

q: What is the relation of residential structures and people to a given area?
n: Density is the relation of dwellings or people to a given land area, as dwelling units or persons per hectare. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, definitions; Chapin & Kaiser, Urban Land Use Planning.

q: What turned early nomads into village dwellers and later city builders?
n: Agricultural surplus let early nomads settle in villages, and freed people for specialized work that led to cities. Source: Childe, The Urban Revolution (1950); Mumford, The City in History.

q: What is the first university town?
n: Of the choices, Vienna has the oldest university, the University of Vienna (1365), the oldest in the German-speaking world. Paris's university dates from about 1150, so the attribution is debatable. Karlsruhe and Versailles are planned court cities. Source: University of Vienna history; Encyclopaedia Britannica.

q: Which is regarded as the oldest city in the history of settlement?
n: Eridu in southern Mesopotamia (founded about 5400 BC) is regarded in Sumerian tradition and archaeology as the oldest city. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Eridu; Kostof, The City Shaped.

q: Which is among the oldest continuously inhabited cities?
n: Damascus is among the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world, occupied since at least the 3rd millennium BC. Source: UNESCO (Ancient City of Damascus).

q: Which Roman forum type was laid out with strict formality?
n: The Imperial Fora of Rome (Caesar, Augustus, Trajan) were laid out with strict axial symmetry and formality, unlike the irregular Republican Forum Romanum. Source: Fletcher, A History of Architecture; Encyclopaedia Britannica.

q: Who is the first noted urban planner, famous for replanning Miletus?
n: Hippodamus of Miletus is the first noted urban planner. He is associated with the gridded replanning of Miletus after 479 BC. Source: Aristotle, Politics II; Encyclopaedia Britannica.

q: The first city that signified the rise of the church, with the church being an integral part of its urban design.
n: Constantinople, refounded by Constantine in 330 as a Christian capital, made churches (Hagia Sophia, Holy Apostles) integral to its urban design. It signified the rise of the church in city planning. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Constantinople; Kostof, The City Shaped.

q: What were the military towns of Spanish colonial settlement called?
n: In Spanish colonial settlement, presidios were the fortified military towns or garrisons. Pueblos were civil towns and missions religious ones. Source: Laws of the Indies; Reps, Town Planning in Frontier America.

q: Which development is the icon of 1950s middle-class suburbanization in Metro Manila?
n: Philamlife Homes in Quezon City (1950s) is the icon of postwar middle-class suburbanization in Metro Manila. Source: Lico, Arkitekturang Filipino; Quezon City heritage records.

q: Which Metro Manila city is largest in land area?
n: Quezon City is the largest Metro Manila city by land area, about 166 km². Source: PSA; Quezon City Government.

q: Which model by Ernest Burgess sees the city as five rings around the CBD?
n: Ernest Burgess's concentric zone model (Chicago, 1925) describes the city as five rings around the CBD. Source: Park, Burgess & McKenzie, The City (1925).

q: Which land use planning stresses managing land so this generation benefits without compromising future ones?
n: Sustainable land use planning manages land so the present generation benefits without compromising future generations. Source: Brundtland Report, Our Common Future (1987); DHSUD CLUP Guidebook.

q: Which term describes urban settlement fully confined within the city's legal limits and fully occupied?
n: A true bounded city is one whose urban settlement fills its legal limits exactly, fully occupied with no overspill or rural land. Source: Gallion & Eisner, The Urban Pattern; urban geography texts.

q: What planning covers roads, bridges, schools, parking, public buildings, water and waste facilities?
n: Capital facilities planning programs public infrastructure (roads, bridges, schools, parking, public buildings, water and waste facilities) through a capital improvement program. Source: APA Planning and Urban Design Standards.

q: What is a place with a large concentration of people having urban traits?
n: A city is a place with a large, dense concentration of people with urban characteristics. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, city.

q: What is a long, deep, narrow valley cut by running water?
n: A ravine is a long, deep, narrow valley cut by running water, smaller than a canyon. Source: Merriam-Webster; Encyclopaedia Britannica.

q: What is a very steep face of rock or clay?
n: A cliff is a very steep or vertical face of rock or clay. A cliff differs from a slope in being nearly vertical, often formed by erosion or faulting. Source: Merriam-Webster.

q: What is a long, narrow chain of hills or mountains?
n: A ridge is a long, narrow chain of hills or mountains, or the crest of one. Source: Merriam-Webster.

q: What are angles measured clockwise from a meridian, usually north?
n: Azimuths are horizontal angles measured clockwise from a reference meridian, usually north (some geodetic systems use south). Source: Davis & Foote, Surveying: Theory and Practice.

q: Which field between planning and architecture deals with large-scale city organization and the space between buildings, not individual buildings?
n: Urban design sits between planning and architecture. It deals with the large-scale organization of the city and the spaces between buildings, not individual buildings. Source: Barnett, An Introduction to Urban Design; APA Planning and Urban Design Standards.

q: The orderly arrangement of urban streets and public spaces.
n: City planning is the orderly arrangement of a city's streets, public spaces and land uses. Source: Merriam-Webster; Branch, Comprehensive City Planning.

q: Which 20th-century problem is rapid outward growth that consumes nearby rural land?
n: Urban sprawl is rapid, low-density outward growth that consumes nearby rural land. It was a defining 20th-century urban problem. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, urban sprawl.

q: What development meets present needs without compromising future generations?
n: Sustainable development meets the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet theirs. Source: Brundtland Report, Our Common Future (1987).

q: What is marked by higher density and more built features than its surroundings?
n: An urban center is an area with higher density and more built features than its surroundings. Source: Urban geography texts; PSA urban classification.

q: What is a contiguous piece of land under one ownership, recorded as a single unit?
n: A parcel is a contiguous piece of land under one ownership, recorded as a single unit. Source: PD 1529; Black's Law Dictionary.

q: Which theory deals with the geographic location of economic activity?
n: Location theory (Weber, Lösch, Christaller) explains the geographic location of economic activities. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, location theory.

q: What is an improved way between two places for vehicles and other land travel?
n: A road is an improved way between two places for vehicles and other land travel. Source: DPWH; Merriam-Webster.

q: Niemeyer believed that relating large areas to each other is freedom, as in the planned city of __.
n: Niemeyer's planned city was Brasília, which is not among the choices (New Orleans, Germany, Chicago), so "none of the above" is correct. Source: UNESCO (Brasília); Niemeyer, The Curves of Time.

q: What is the rapid rise in human population from higher births, lower infant mortality and longer life?
n: A population explosion is a rapid rise in population from higher births, lower infant mortality and longer life expectancy. Source: Weeks, Population: An Introduction.

q: Which term means land suitable for crops and livestock?
n: Agricultural land is the legal and planning term for land suitable for crops and livestock. Source: RA 6657 (CARL), Sec. 3(c).

q: Which planning investigates people's and communities' needs and translates them into policy and action?
n: Social planning studies the needs of people and communities and translates them into policies, programs and action. Source: Branch, Comprehensive City Planning.

q: In statistics, what is studied to analyze the characteristics or changes of people in an area?
n: Population is the statistical subject studied to analyze the characteristics of people in an area and how they change. Source: PSA; Weeks, Population: An Introduction.

q: What are Lynch's five elements of the city image?
n: Kevin Lynch's five elements of the city image are paths, edges, districts, nodes and landmarks. Source: Lynch, The Image of the City (1960).

q: Consideration on sidewalks.
n: Sidewalk width is set mainly by the volume of people (pedestrian flow) it must carry, its level of service. Source: Fruin, Pedestrian Planning and Design; Highway Capacity Manual.

q: Which is a form of mass transit?
n: A bus is a form of mass transit, carrying many riders on fixed routes. Taxis, company cars and carpools are private or paratransit. Source: Vuchic, Urban Transit Systems and Technology.

q: An urban utopia, idealized and imagined, is what kind of model?
n: A normative model describes how things ought to be, so an idealized urban utopia is a normative model. Source: Lynch, Good City Form.

q: Why did Chicago build high-rises in the late 1800s?
o: High land cost in the Loop
n: Chicago built high-rises in the 1880s–90s because land in the Loop was scarce and costly. Steel frames and elevators made it pay to build upward. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Chicago School; Condit, The Chicago School of Architecture.

q: What is the main function of zoning?
n: Zoning's main function is controlling land use: what may be built where, and its bulk and density. Source: HLURB/DHSUD Model Zoning Ordinance; APA Planning and Urban Design Standards.

q: Who brought the idea of the region into planning and coined "conurbation"?
n: Patrick Geddes brought the region into planning (survey before plan) and coined "conurbation" in Cities in Evolution (1915). Source: Geddes, Cities in Evolution.

q: Which Greek architect-planner described cities as urban nightmares of clogged arteries, pollution and poor services?
n: C.A. Doxiadis, Greek planner and founder of ekistics, described modern cities as urban nightmares of clogged arteries, pollution and failing services. Source: Doxiadis, Ekistics (1968).

q: Who wrote Garden Cities of To-morrow?
n: Ebenezer Howard wrote Garden Cities of To-morrow (1902), first published as To-morrow: A Peaceful Path to Real Reform (1898). Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Ebenezer Howard.

q: Who is known for the concept of urban design that emphasizes the relationship between people and the environment, focusing on pedestrian-scale cities?
n: Kevin Lynch is known for urban design centred on how people perceive and relate to their environment, at the pedestrian scale of the city. Source: Lynch, The Image of the City; Good City Form.
